body:
## Problem

The aggregator and API services communicate through shared JSON files on disk. There is no formal contract defining the shape, semantics, or evolution of this data exchange. A change to the aggregator's output format (adding a field, changing a timestamp format, renaming a key) can silently break the API until someone notices incorrect responses. When both services are deployed independently, there is no safety net.

## Requirements

- **Bi-directional contract testing with PactFlow** — Set up Pact as the contract testing framework. The aggregator acts as the provider (publishes price data), the API acts as the consumer (reads price data). Contracts define exact request/response shapes for: fetching current prices, fetching historical prices, fetching source metadata, and WebSocket price stream messages.
- **Consumer-driven contracts** — The API service (consumer) defines what it expects from the aggregator (provider). The aggregator must verify that it satisfies all active consumer contracts before deployment. Multiple consumers (API, future webhook service, future analytics pipeline) each define their own contracts.
- **Provider verification with canary deployments** — When the aggregator deploys, a canary instance runs provider verification against all consumer contracts pulled from PactFlow. If verification fails, the canary is rolled back automatically and the incident is posted to Slack/PagerDuty.
- **Contract versioning and compatibility gates** — Every contract is versioned. PactFlow's `pactflow.publish` captures the full matrix of consumer-provider compatibilities. CI enforces backward compatibility: a consumer change that breaks existing providers is rejected unless all providers are also updated.
- **WebSocket message contract testing** — Pact's message pact support is used to test WebSocket message shapes. The API defines expected message formats for price updates, heartbeat, backfill-batch, and error messages. The aggregator verifies it produces matching messages.
- **Automated contract diff review** — On every PR that modifies a contract, PactFlow posts a diff of the contract changes to the PR as a comment. Human reviewers can see exactly which interactions changed and whether the change is backward compatible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PactFlow integrated into both services
- [ ] Consumer-driven contracts for: current prices, history, sources, WS messages
- [ ] Provider verification with canary rollback on failure
- [ ] Contract versioning with backward-compatibility enforcement in CI
- [ ] WebSocket message pacts for all message types
- [ ] Contract diff review posted to PRs automatically
- [ ] PactFlow matrix showing all consumer-provider compatibilities
- [ ] Negative tests: breaking a contract triggers rollback, posted to Slack
title: Bi-directional Pact contract testing with canary verification, WS message pacts, and automated compatibility gates
